title: EvalRelay: staged evaluation orchestration for catalog + tenant pin upgrades
creator: Ravi Menon
description: Problem: When a model version is pinned or upgraded (catalog-wide or customer-locked), we lack a standardized, automated way to run a sequence of targeted evals and produce an actionable impact assessment. Current ad-hoc probes either miss tenant-specific regressions or incur unnecessary cost when run broadly. Goal: Build 'EvalRelay', an orchestration service that automatically triggers a staged evaluation pipeline on pin/upgrade events for both catalog and tenant-pinned models. EvalRelay will run progressive checks (fast smoke, tenant-weighted canary, sampled fidelity probes), compute an impact score combining quality deltas, traffic exposure, and cost delta, and provide clear signals (pass, warn, fail) plus a recommended action (promote, monitor, rollback). The system must respect budget guards, tenant SLAs, and allow explicit opt-outs per-catalog or per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: On catalog pin event, EvalRelay schedules and runs a fast smoke suite within 5 minutes for high-priority models (catalog tier 'critical').
On tenant pin event, EvalRelay automatically selects a tenant-specific prompt set and runs a targeted canary sample representative of that tenant's traffic profile within 10 minutes.
EvalRelay computes a normalized impact score (0-100) combining quality delta, traffic proportion, and cost delta and stores it in the audit log.
If impact score exceeds configurable threshold for 'fail', EvalRelay marks the pin as 'blocked-recommendation:rollback' and creates a Slack alert + incident channel recommendation.
Budget-aware sampling: system enforces tenant- and org-level eval spend caps and falls back to lighter probes when budget constrained, with clear annotations in the evaluation report.
APIs: team can query /evalrelay/status and receive staged progress, per-step logs, and final verdict; Console surfaces a rollout panel with live progress and rollback advice.
All triggered evaluations produce pinned artifacts: test inputs, outputs, diffs, and links to GitHub PRs or Deploy records for traceability.
Security review and data retention policy completed before release (security_review_required = true).
success_metrics: Detect regressions prior to 90% of customer-impacting pin-related incidents (baseline: current detection rate ~30%).
Reduce mean time to detect pin regressions from days to < 1 hour for high-traffic customers.
Keep additional eval cost increase under 12% for organization-level upgrades through sampling efficiency and budget guards.
>90% of automated recommendations align with human reviewer decision in first 6 weeks (measured on audits).
implementation_notes: Architecture: EvalRelay is an event-driven service listening to catalog change stream and tenant pin webhook events; it fans out jobs to existing eval runner with staged policies.
Staging: three evaluation stages - 1) Fast smoke (synthetic, cheap), 2) Tenant-weighted canary (real prompts sampled), 3) Broad lightweight fidelity probes (larger sample, lower frequency).

Impact scoring: combine normalized metrics - quality delta (AUC/Rouge/F1 where applicable), unexpected token-level hallucination metrics, traffic-weight multiplier, and cost-per-token delta; weightings configurable per-project.
Budgeting: integrate with cost-control service to check remaining eval budget; if near limit, automatically reduce sample sizes or queue lower-priority probes.
Observability: emit structured events for each stage (start/complete/fail) to internal tracing and build a console timeline widget; add 'evalrelay' dashboards to Console default views.
APIs: read endpoints for status and raw artifacts, and webhook callbacks for external integrations (Slack, PagerDuty).
Data privacy: tenant-specific prompt sets are masked for shared reports; raw artifacts remain in tenant-scoped encrypted storage for audit duration.
Permissions: pin-triggered evals must check caller permissions; tenant can opt-out or restrict evals via tenant settings.
Rollback flow: the service should create a recommended rollback PR/command and an explicit human-approval action for automated rollbacks (initial rollout will only recommend, not auto-rollback).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: evals could amplify costs on large catalog rollouts - Mitigation: enforce progressive rollout and cost caps, default lightweight probes for catalog-wide promotions.
Risk: false positives due to metric variance - Mitigation: use historical baselines and statistical significance checks before marking 'fail'.
Risk: tenant data leakage in cross-tenant reports - Mitigation: mask prompts in shared views and restrict raw artifact access to tenant owners and security.

Risk: delayed feedback loops for very low-traffic tenants - Mitigation: include synthetic probes focused on tenant-critical workflows and increase sampling weight for slow-traffic tenants when scheduled.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): implement EvalRelay and enable for internal catalog and a set of 5 pilot tenants; recommend-only rollbacks; run for 4 weeks.
Phase 2 (selected customers): open beta for customers who opt-in; add console UI for rollout progress; collect feedback and tune scoring weights.

Phase 3 (default): enable automated recommendations for all catalog pins and tenant pins, with strict budget defaults and ability to opt-out; consider automated rollback after SLA and trust thresholds met.
Phase 4 (optimizations): add traffic-aware dynamic sampling, cost-saving caching for repeated prompts, and integration with release orchestration for one-click rollback.
